finding: For any fixed admissible odd box and nodes a<t1<t2<b<t3<t4<c<t5<d, existence of a single xi in [t3,t4] whose nonnegative-coefficient even numerator gives positive pairing on all eight odd-moment-boundary rays, uniformly over every stable even interval box and arbitrary actual members, is exactly one finite LP with 16 sets of 14 nonnegative Motzkin multipliers. Feasibility proves no direct strictly-negative-coordinate certificate on that fixed data; infeasibility rules out only this stronger uniform selector family. The 16 cases combine two four-node supports, four omitted odd moments and two possible worst middle odd endpoints. Strict mixed-envelope identities supply an explicit nonvacuous example and open neighborhood. This characterization does not prove uniform feasibility across all input boxes or the original five-frequency/unrestricted SPR7 verdict.

remaining_gap: The LP has not been proved feasible for every admissible odd box and tuple, nor shown infeasible for one; other direct-certificate phase placements, larger support and the original unrestricted problem remain open.
